newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: WTO confirms China entry talks next week.
newsitem.headline: WTO confirms China entry talks next week.

text.p: China and its major trading partners will hold three-day talks in Geneva next week on Beijing's bid to join the World Trade Orgnisation (WTO), a WTO spokesman confirmed on Friday.

Long Yongtu, assistant foreign trade minister, will lead China's delegation in informal bilateral talks on Wednesday, Thursday and Friday morning with key powers -- including the United States, the European Union and Japan.
Long has been in Brussels discussing market access issues with EU officials, according to diplomats.

A formal session of the WTO working party, which is negotiating Beijing's terms of entry to the 131 member trade watchdog, is set for Friday afternoon (1300GT), the WTO spokesman told a news briefing.
The negotiations began more than a decade ago, but partners including the United States and European Union are seeking greater concessions.
Renato Ruggiero, WTO's director-general who travelled to Beijing last month, urged Chinese leaders to polish up their market-opening offers.

At the last round of WTO talks in March, both sides said that progress had been made. Long announced at the time that China would grant all companies, including wholly-owned foreign firms, the right to import and export after a three-year transitional period following its accession to the WTO.
Trade diplomats expect another WTO session in July and if all goes smoothly for China to be admitted next year.
